title: Which quadratic families have maximal prime runs, and what discriminants do they correspond to?
statement: n^2+n+q has a full prime run for n=0..q-2 exactly when q in {2,3,5,11,17,41}, corresponding to Heegner discriminants -7,-11,-19,-43,-67,-163 (Rabinowitsch 1913). Generalize: for other quadratic families an^2+bn+c, characterize maximal prime runs and their discriminant correspondence.
why: Directly extends the result the arena already derived. Classical theory exists for the principal form; the computational question of which families give long runs and whether the correspondence is as clean is concrete and checkable.

title: Is the list of 65 idoneal numbers complete?
statement: Euler's idoneal numbers: n such that x^2+ny^2 represents a number in essentially one way only when that number is prime, a prime power, or twice one. 65 are known, largest 1848. Conjectured complete; at most one more can exist, and none under GRH.
why: Genuinely open, same circle of ideas as the Heegner correspondence, and computationally explorable. Any structural constraint found on a hypothetical 66th is real.

title: Does phi(n) | n-1 force n prime?
statement: Lehmer's totient problem: if phi(n) divides n-1, must n be prime? No composite example is known. Known constraints: a counterexample must be odd, squarefree, and have at least 15 prime factors.
why: Constraint-tightening is tractable in hours even though the search space is astronomically out of reach. The value is retiring structure, not finding n.

title: Is Giuga's congruence prime-exclusive?
statement: Giuga: n is prime iff sum_{k=1}^{n-1} k^(n-1) = -1 mod n. The forward direction is Fermat; the converse is open. A counterexample must be a Carmichael-like number satisfying strong joint conditions.
why: The counterexample conditions are checkable and compose with Carmichael structure. Good target for constraint derivation.

title: Are 4, 5, 7 the only n with n!+1 a perfect square?
statement: Brocard's problem: n!+1 = m^2 has known solutions n=4,5,7 (m=5,11,71). Searched past 10^9 with none further.
why: Modular obstructions are cheap to compute and the search-space retirement is honest even though a full search is hopeless.

title: Is the multiplicity of an integer in Pascal's triangle bounded?
statement: Singmaster's conjecture: there is an absolute bound on how many times an integer >1 appears in Pascal's triangle. 3003 appears 8 times; no number is known to appear more.
why: Multiplicity-8 numbers come from simultaneous binomial identities tied to Fibonacci-like recurrences. Concrete search with real structure to find.

title: FORGE: generate and break conjectures about polynomial prime-run records
statement: Search wide families of integer polynomials for prime-run records, form the sharpest conjecture the data supports, then attack that conjecture rather than defending it.
why: Nobody has looked at most of this space. A forged conjecture that breaks in ten minutes cost ten minutes; one that survives is a small real result.

title: FORGE: fixed points and cycles of digit-power maps in mixed bases
statement: Maps like n -> sum of d-th powers of base-b digits have known cycles for b=10. Explore other bases and exponents, conjecture cycle-structure laws from the data, then try to falsify them.
why: Cheap to compute exhaustively below the natural bound, so conjectures can be settled rather than merely supported.

title: FORGE: structure in aliquot sequence behaviour
statement: Aliquot sequences (iterate sum of proper divisors) either terminate, cycle, or are open. Look for statistical or structural regularities, conjecture, and attack.
why: Large open catalogue, and driver-based heuristics give real structure to conjecture about.

title: FORGE: primality density in low-order integer recurrences
statement: For families like a(n+1)=k*a(n)+m, look for parameter choices with anomalous prime density, conjecture a law, then break it.
why: Enormous unexplored parameter space with cheap evaluation.
